cases.purpose: Observe setsid through kernel PTY/session state in a live, handshaken child.
cases.oracle: An independent Python os.setsid and Linux TIOCSCTTY participant supplies the reference; the parent verifies /proc descriptors, session IDs, controlling-device identity and tcgetpgrp on the fixture-owned PTYs.

cases.purpose: A separate owned process group becomes foreground and the original group is restored.
cases.oracle: The reference uses os.setpgid and tcsetpgrp on the VM driver’s fresh controlling PTY; the independent driver samples tcgetpgrp and process signal masks.
cases.comparison: The PTY driver observes the foreground group while the owned child is alive, then requires the restoring marker and a clean exit.
cases.candidate_script:
set -m
/usr/bin/sleep 5 &
job=$!
trap 'kill "$job" 2>/dev/null || :; wait "$job" 2>/dev/null || :' EXIT
trap '' TTOU
pty foreground "$job" 0 || exit 1
printf 'FOREGROUND-READY\n'
IFS= read -r -t 1.5 _ < <(/usr/bin/sleep 1.5) || :
pty foreground "$$" 0 || exit 1
printf 'FOREGROUND-RESTORED\n'
cases.reference_script:
/usr/bin/python3 -c '
import os, signal, subprocess, time
signal.signal(signal.SIGTTOU, signal.SIG_IGN)
child = subprocess.Popen(["/usr/bin/sleep", "5"], preexec_fn=lambda: os.setpgid(0, 0))
try:
    os.tcsetpgrp(0, child.pid)
    print("FOREGROUND-READY", flush=True)
    time.sleep(1.5)
    os.tcsetpgrp(0, os.getpgrp())
    print("FOREGROUND-RESTORED", flush=True)
finally:
    child.terminate()
    child.wait(timeout=3)
'
